features.name: any_counterargument_over_twice_op_length
features.definition: Is at least one counter-argument comment more than twice as many words as the OP's argument?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads into a list of strings; unparseable or missing -> null. Word count = len(text.split()) on the string. OP word count = len(argument.split()) on the current argument column (title excluded). If argument is missing or has 0 words -> null. Empty comment list -> 0. Otherwise 1 if any comment has word count > 2 * OP word count (strictly greater), else 0. Raw-text count: no semantic filtering; text may contain edits or outcome announcements.

h0: any_counterargument_over_twice_op_length has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
h1: Rows with at least one counter-argument more than twice the length of the OP's argument are more likely to have delta=1.
note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP view change); association only, not causal. Length is whitespace-delimited word count. The hypothesis is about individual counter-arguments; the row-level feature is the "any" version, and it does not identify which comment persuaded (no per-comment outcomes). The OC_comments list is only the available comments; the argument text is current text and may include edits or delta announcements, and comments may too (raw text, not outcome-free). log_length not used because its construction is undocumented and it is not equivalent to word count. Rows with zero-word arguments yield null.
